questions.q: Which depreciation method type looks up a predefined rate using an asset's life and year of life, rather than calculating a fresh formula each period?
questions.explain: Table-based methods pull a published rate from a table based on life and year of life — how many accelerated tax schedules like MACRS are implemented.

questions.q: A $120,000 asset with a $20,000 salvage value and a 10-year life is depreciated straight-line. What is the annual depreciation?
questions.explain: ($120,000 - $20,000) / 10 = $10,000 per year, the depreciable basis spread evenly across the useful life.

questions.q: Why does a flat-rate method applied to net book value produce a declining depreciation charge each year?
options: Because the rate itself decreases every year
Because the rate is applied to a shrinking balance each period
Because flat-rate methods always use a shorter life than straight-line
Because flat-rate methods don't depreciate in the final year
questions.explain: The percentage rate stays fixed, but it's multiplied by the asset's net book value, which shrinks every period — producing a front-loaded, declining pattern.

questions.q: Which depreciation method type is most appropriate for a mining excavator whose wear tracks tonnage moved rather than calendar time?
questions.explain: Units of production ties depreciation to actual usage — tonnage, hours, or miles — rather than the simple passage of time.

options: Net book value plus accumulated depreciation
The invoice amount paid to the vendor including tax
questions.explain: Depreciable basis is the amount actually spread across the asset's useful life: its cost minus its estimated salvage value.
